verdict.rationale: Zulip's source is publicly hosted on GitHub, where the project invites code contributions, and the self-hosted build is the same software that runs Zulip Cloud. The open-license part rests only on community statements that it is open sourced and '100% FOSS', so license coverage is incomplete. missing for 10: a first-party statement naming the specific open-source license, and first-party docs confirming the full codebase (including the Cloud product) is under that license.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: Contributing code. Check out our guide for new contributors to get started.
When you self-host Zulip, you get the same software as our Zulip Cloud customers.
Zulip is my favorite modern chat program because it's actually 100% FOSS, unlike Mattermost and RocketChat, which are only 'open core'.
Good to see it be open sourced.
